questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

During a group discussion, one student says, "Our opening needs to explain the topic before we give examples." Which response best shows active listening?

answer.text: A. That is obvious, so we should move on.

feedback.text: This dismisses the speaker instead of showing understanding. Active listening should show that the listener heard the idea and is willing to work with it.

answer.text: B. You think the audience needs the main idea first. What should we explain in the opening?

feedback.text: Correct. This paraphrases the idea and asks a useful follow-up question, which supports collaborative communication.

answer.text: C. I already wrote my part, so I do not want to change anything.

feedback.text: This focuses only on the listener's own work. Collaboration requires responding to the group's shared goal.

answer.text: D. We should ignore examples completely.

feedback.text: This changes the meaning of the speaker's idea. The speaker wanted better order, not removal of examples.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which action is the clearest example of collaboration during speech planning?

answer.text: A. Choosing the topic alone and telling the group later.

feedback.text: This leaves out the group and does not support a shared decision. Collaboration requires participation from others.

answer.text: B. Waiting silently while others do all the planning.

feedback.text: Silence alone is not collaboration. A group member should listen and contribute when appropriate.

answer.text: C. Correcting every person immediately before they finish speaking.

feedback.text: Interrupting blocks listening and can shut down ideas. A collaborative speaker allows ideas to be completed.

answer.text: D. Asking each group member for ideas and helping combine them into one plan.

feedback.text: Correct. This includes others, listens to ideas, and helps the group move toward a shared plan.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

A listener says, "So you are saying our speech needs more practice before we record it." What active listening skill is the listener using?

answer.text: A. Paraphrasing the speaker's idea

feedback.text: Correct. The listener restates the idea in their own words to check understanding before responding.

answer.text: B. Changing the subject

feedback.text: The listener stays with the speaker's idea. Changing the subject would move away from the message.

answer.text: C. Attacking the speaker

feedback.text: The listener does not insult or blame the speaker. The response focuses on understanding the idea.

answer.text: D. Ending the discussion

feedback.text: The listener is keeping the discussion open by checking meaning.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

In an online class discussion, a student is confused about the task. Which response best supports social and instructional communication?

answer.text: A. You should already know what to do.

feedback.text: This response is dismissive and does not help the student understand the task.

answer.text: B. I am finished, so this is not my problem.

feedback.text: This ignores the communication need. Social and instructional communication should help clarify school tasks.

answer.text: C. The task asks us to give one idea and one reason. I can show where the directions say that.

feedback.text: Correct. This response explains the task and points to the directions, which supports understanding.

answer.text: D. Just write anything quickly.

feedback.text: This may lead to incomplete work. Helpful communication should clarify expectations, not encourage guessing.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L01_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.10

Which response best uses academic communication during a group speech discussion?

answer.text: A. Your idea is bad.

feedback.text: This is too vague and personal. Academic communication should focus on ideas and reasons.

answer.text: B. I understand your point, but I think the evidence should come before the example because the audience needs context.

feedback.text: Correct. This response uses clear academic language, gives a reason, and keeps the focus on the speech.

answer.text: C. Whatever, do it your way.

feedback.text: This avoids communication instead of helping the group make a reasoned decision.

answer.text: D. I do not care about the audience.

feedback.text: This ignores the purpose of communication. Speakers should consider audience understanding.
